summary: Iter30 — Passwordless-invite + auto invite-link E2E verification. BACKEND: 18/18 pytest pass in 6.67s (/app/backend/tests/test_iteration30.py) covering every acceptance criterion — passwordless create (200 + passwordless=true + invite_token, then email/password login returns 401); password+phone create still returns invite_token; passwordless without phone → 400; passwordless with short phone → 400; GET /auth/invite/{token} (public) returns {name, phone_masked (last-4), company}; invalid token → 404; POST /auth/invite/{token}/start returns {phone, name, dev_mode:true, dev_otp:'######'} → OTP verify returns {token, user, tenant} and token works against /auth/me; POST /users/{id}/invite regenerates token (new token != old, old becomes 404); regenerate for phoneless user → 400; regenerate for unknown user → 404; GET /users leak-guard confirms no invite_token or invite_expires_at in list projection; RBAC: sales (no team_manage) blocked with 403 on both /users create and /users/{id}/invite; owner OTP regression on 9820010001 still works. FRONTEND (Playwright, 4 owner UI flows all pass): owner_login PASS; nav_to_people PASS; B_add_passwordless_shows_invite_modal PASS (login-method-otp toggle hides member-password-input, shows passwordless-hint, save → invite-link-modal appears with invite-link-input containing '/login?invite=<token>', copy-invite-link visible, invite-whatsapp-share href starts with 'https://wa.me'); C_password_with_phone_modal PASS (password-mode member with phone ALSO surfaces invite-link-modal, matching the review spec 'response also has invite_token'); D_per_row_regenerate PASS (invite-link-<userId> row buttons render for every non-owner with a phone, click regenerates a fresh token via POST /users/{id}/invite and opens the same modal — 11 buttons found, first click succeeded). CRITICAL BUG FOUND on the /login?invite=<token> deep-link: two concurrent invite/start requests race due to React.StrictMode double-invoking the empty-deps useEffect in Login.js, producing TWO different dev_otps; the one shown to the user does NOT always match the one persisted last in db.otp_codes (upsert-by-phone), so 'Verify & sign in' returns 401 'Incorrect OTP'. Reproduced in 2/2 clean runs of the Playwright test with fresh members. Backend proven correct via curl-parallel test — issue is exclusively the frontend double-fire.

ui_bugs.issue: React.StrictMode (index.js) causes the empty-deps useEffect to run twice in dev; two concurrent POST /auth/invite/{token}/start requests each generate a distinct dev_otp; whichever setOtpCode call fires last wins in React state, but whichever request upserts last wins in db.otp_codes — these are NOT guaranteed to be the same request. On mismatch, clicking otp-submit-button returns 401 Incorrect OTP. Reproduced deterministically in 2/2 runs.

integration_issues.flow: Invite deep-link → auto-OTP → verify & sign in
integration_issues.issue: Displayed auto-filled OTP does not always match the OTP the backend expects → user sees 'Incorrect OTP' despite the code being auto-filled by the app itself.

action_items: Login.js — guard the invite useEffect against StrictMode double-invocation. Simple fix: `const startedRef = useRef(false); useEffect(() => { if (startedRef.current) return; startedRef.current = true; ... }, []);` OR gate on a state flag OR move invite handling into a `useMemo`-style once-per-token guard keyed by the token string. Without this, the /login?invite=<token> flow reliably fails in dev (webpack-dev-server) despite backend being correct. Note: In a production build StrictMode does NOT double-invoke effects, so the bug is masked in prod builds — but the preview URL served here is `yarn start` (dev), so end-users hitting the preview see the bug.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1025-1062 create_user is clean — correct order of guards (role validity → email uniqueness → password/phone rules → hash → insert → invite_token only if valid phone). Returns invite_token in the CREATE response but subsequent /users list projection strips it (line 1021) — verified via TestListUsersLeakGuard. Good separation.

server.py:1065-1077 regenerate_invite correctly requires team_manage, 404 on wrong tenant/user (via tenant_id filter in find_one), 400 without a valid 10-digit phone. Returns only the new token+name+phone_masked — does NOT return phone or full user, minimizing leakage. Verified.

server.py:905-935 invite_info + invite_start are public (no auth dep) and correctly separate 'peek at invite' from 'issue OTP'. Both 404 on unknown token; both 410 on expired. invite_start calls _issue_otp with enforce_cooldown=False — appropriate since the invitee typically clicks the link exactly once and the 30s cooldown would break that first-time flow. HOWEVER: because cooldown is disabled here, the StrictMode double-fire bug on the frontend is amplified — every concurrent frontend call successfully upserts a NEW code.

Login.js:71-89 useEffect empty-deps + StrictMode dev double-invoke is the RCA. The IIFE inside is not idempotent (it calls setOtpCode with whatever value comes back from a network round-trip). Fix with a ref-guard (as above) or by keying on token: `useEffect(() => { let cancelled = false; ... if (cancelled) return; ... return () => { cancelled = true; }; }, [])` — but the cancel-guard alone doesn't help here because BOTH effect bodies have already dispatched requests before cleanup fires. Only a ref-guard prevents the second setup from firing the request at all.

Login.js:83 UX nit — on error, the toast.info 'Dev OTP: XXXXXX (auto-filled)' still shows the FIRST call's code even though state ended up with the SECOND. The mismatch is visible if you compare the toast text with the input value in some runs.

Team.js:82,85 MemberDialog.save() correctly branches on form.passwordless — passwordless path omits password, non-passwordless includes password. Both surface the returned invite_token via onInvite. Verified.

Team.js:191-198 getInviteLink calls POST /users/{id}/invite — no local phone check, relies on server 400. Since the button is only rendered when u.phone exists (line 233 `{u.phone && (...)}`), this is fine in practice.

AuthContext.loginWithOtp reuses persist() — post-OTP token is stored under the same dos_token key as email/password login, so the passwordless member's session behaves identically to a regular one. No branching.

Server-side race amplifier: /auth/invite/{token}/start with enforce_cooldown=False allows unlimited back-to-back OTP overwrites. Consider adding a lightweight in-flight guard (5s dedupe by token or phone) OR only regenerating a code if the current one is > N seconds old — masks any client double-fire and reduces attack surface for OTP spam via public endpoint. Non-blocking but worth considering.

rca of the issue: Race condition — React.StrictMode dev-mode double-invocation of Login.js:72-89 useEffect causes two concurrent POST /auth/invite/{token}/start network calls. Each returns a distinct 6-digit dev_otp. React state ends with whichever setOtpCode fires last (last-write-wins in state batching). MongoDB db.otp_codes upsert-by-phone ends with whichever DB write commits last. These two orderings are independent → ~50% mismatch → 'Incorrect OTP' on Verify. Reproduction: (1) create a passwordless member (owner_token, /api/users), (2) open /login?invite=<invite_token>, (3) wait for otp-code-input to auto-fill (6 digits), (4) click otp-submit-button → auth-error becomes 'Incorrect OTP' (401 from /api/auth/otp/verify). Mitigation for user: click 'Resend OTP' once (which invokes a fresh single request in the click handler, non-StrictMode-double-invoked path) — then Verify. Real fix in main agent scope.
